04 / REFLECT

Free journal

NO FILTER

Use this space however you need. A brain dump, a good moment, something you're worried about, or a thought you can't quite shake.

Need a starting point?

What has been harder than people around me might realise?
When did I feel most like myself today?
What do I wish I could say out loud?
What would I say to a bandmate who felt the way I do?
What do I need more of — and what do I need less of?

Take a minute

PAUSE / RESET

A short breathing pause can help you create a little space between the moment and your next move. Keep it comfortable; return to normal breathing whenever you need.

Ready when you areFollow the gentle pace for one minute.

Ground yourself

5–4–3–2–1

Look around and gently notice:

5 things you can see
4 things you can feel
3 things you can hear
2 things you can smell
1 thing you can taste — or one slow breath you can notice

A few things worth remembering

Rest is part of the work. You don't have to earn it.
A difficult day is not a failed tour.
You are allowed to change the plan.
You can care about the show and still care about yourself.
You don't need to be “on” all the time.

Your privacy comes first

PRIVATE BY DEFAULT

Your entries stay in this browser on this device. This journal does not send your writing to ChatGPT, OpenAI or Fit For The Pit automatically. There is no account, tracking pixel or analytics in this standalone journal.

Sharing is always your choice. Select an entry below and choose “Prepare email”. Your email app will open with that entry addressed to fftpit@gmail.com. Nothing is sent until you review it and press Send.

Only the entry you select, your name and any email address you choose to provide will be included. Do not share anything you would prefer to keep private. Email is not an end-to-end private journal storage method: once sent, the information is handled by your email provider and Fit For The Pit.

Your wellbeing matters

This journal is designed to work locally in your browser. It does not connect to ChatGPT or OpenAI, and does not automatically transmit your entries. Your browser stores entries on this device; anyone with access to this browser profile or device may be able to view them. This journal is a reflection tool, not a medical service or a substitute for professional mental health support. You can skip any prompt that doesn't feel helpful. If things feel overwhelming, reach out to someone you trust or a qualified professional. If you may be in immediate danger or might harm yourself, contact emergency services now (999 in the UK) or go to A&E. In the UK and Ireland, Samaritans can be called free on 116 123.
